ratings.reasons: The fall-in at the end reads, and nothing leaves the frame now. But the loose phase breaks the hexagram: several yin halves drift toward each other (e.g. +0.35 left with -0.25 right), so in army-48 the gaps close and the top lines look like whole yang bars with a seam. For a few beats a newcomer sees a different, mostly-yang figure, and the 0.2-0.4 drifts read as a rendering glitch more than troops out of rank.
ratings.redo: Keep every yin gap open: move each half outward only, by uneven amounts (0.15 to 0.5, different per half), so the ranks' outer edges go ragged while every line still shows its break, and dim them as now. Then the general brightens and the halves slide back in, nearest first, as in the current fall-in.

ratings.reasons: Now visible: the trigrams close the full gap, an amber seam flashes where lines 3 and 4 touch, and both ease back. It reads as heaven and earth meeting, and it pairs with 12's drift apart.

The upper jaw holds and the lower rises and falls twice, clearly visible. But the whole lower trigram rises as a block until the gap between the trigrams closes (nourish-57), which is almost exactly 11's move of the lower trigram rising to meet the upper, so the two shorts read alike and neither looks like a jaw.
ratings.redo: Close the jaw, not the trigram: the bottom line rises most (about 0.35) and lines 2 and 3 rise less (about 0.2 and 0.1), so the lower lines crowd together as the jaw comes up, while the gap between the trigrams stays open; twice, at the same calm pace. The bottom line moving and the top line still carries the thunder-below, mountain-above reading.

ratings.reasons: The four brightening yang lines and the ends splaying away (top pair opening up, bottom pair opening down, 12 degrees) read at a glance as a middle too heavy for its weak ends, and it no longer looks like drooping wings. The middle lines' spread is slight, but their brightening carries the cause.

The amber starts in the lower centre, takes the yang lines around it, then the upper flame does the same, and all cool back but the two centres: two identical flames one after the other, clinging to what they burn. Clear on a phone and it teaches the doubled trigram.

The glow now shows climbing the five yang (breakthrough-42 lower lines visibly brighter) before the top yin's halves slide off and fade. The five acting together and the last weak line going is readable.
The yin now rises clearly until it meets line 2, which flashes amber (meet-61), and it sinks back dimmer: a small beginning met and held by the line next to it. Visible without the crack.

No line moves; an amber flash runs up the lower trigram from its yang base, then up the upper one, and the hexagram stands still at the end. Calm and readable. Note the docstring says the second flash is fainter but the code calls the same st.flash for both, and the stills show them equal; either scale the second or change the docstring.
The centre opens by 0.45 each way and all four halves stay in frame, while lines 2 and 5 brighten: empty within, firm at the centres. It reads at a glance.
